- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py
  Line or code reference: check_pr_hand_back, lines 481-510
  Problem: When a claude/* PR has mergeable_state == "ditty" (conflicted) but no hand-off comment exists yet, _check_claude_fixer_pr returns None. The function then skips the check-runs block at line 487 (because conficted=True makes `due is None and not conflicted` False) and falls through to line 509-510 which returns `open`. A genuinely conflicted claude/* PR with no hand-off comment is never handed back as a due conflict.
  Why it fails at runtime: If a claude/* PR becomes conflicted after the review workflow already completed (e.g., base branch moved forward between runs) or a force-push creates new conflicts, no new hand-off comment is posted until a new review workflow runs. With no hand-off and no live claim, check_pr_hand_back returns state="open" at line 510 regardless of age or active-runs. The §26 checker and the hourly sweep both call -han-back mode, so neither will ever wake a fixer or start a fresh session for this genuinely conflicted PR. The PR stays open and unreviewed until something else pushes to it or a review workflow is re-dispatched by another mechanism. The old check_pr path (lines 226-252) handled this case by falling through to the age/active-rans check after _check_claude_fixer_pr returned None.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
